title: Daily scratchlist: quant eval + prompt experiments
body:
Quick morning dump (things to try / ephemeral notes). Not polished — my lab notebook for the day.

CONTEXT:
- Week focused on 8-bit q8_0 profiles across chat models; checking perf/quality tradeoffs for short-chat (<=128 tokens) and bursty long-chat (up to 1024).
- Goal: find a config that reduces GPU cycles ~20% while keeping mean BLEU/ROUGE-ish proxy loss change <2%.

TODAY'S PRIORITIES (ordered):
1) Re-run eval set A with q8_0 + KV-cache warm start enabled. Compare to baseline fp16.
2) Prompt set sanity: add system prompt neutralizer for toxicity edge cases.
3) Quick stress: 4 concurrent streams @seq_len=512, batch=4, measure p95 latency.
4) Capture any hallucination spikes on factual QA subset.

EXPERIMENT NOTES / COMMANDS:
- Local command (mini reproduce):
  ./run_eval.sh --model /mnt/models/gpt-like-7b --quant q8_0 --warm-kv true --prompts data/evalA.json --out results/jamie/2026-03-13_q8_0_warm.json
- Use docker image: redwood/infer:dev-202603 (has new scheduler hooks)
- Watchpoints: memory growth > 200MB per step -> abort.

PROMPT SET CHANGES (quick):
- evalA: baseline conversational prompts (customer support style). Add one extra system instruction: "Answer concisely, prefer lower verbosity, cite source sentence index if factual."
- toxicity checks: insert 12 adversarial phrasings from internal list toxic-2025-v2.txt
- few-shot seeding: vary between 0 / 1 / 3 shots for ablation.

QUANT NOTES:
- q8_0 seemed stable on small local tests but KV-cache alignment might be off — check whether cached keys are cast consistently (uint8 vs int8?)
- hypothesis: quant rounding + rotary embedding scale causes drift after ~200 tokens. Try forcing rotary rescale = true in runtime config.
- naive test: run single long sample (1024 tokens) and diff logits against fp16 at steps [50, 150, 300, 512].

OBSERVATIONS (from quick morning run):
- q8_0 + warm-kv: p50 latency down ~14%, p95 down ~9% on short-chat.
- BUT on long-chat warm-kv introduced small token-level divergence at ~180th token (reproducible).
- hallucination count (simple QA heuristics) increased from 1.8% -> 3.1% on factual subset. Not great.

IMMEDIATE ACTIONS:
- [ ] Add logging to dump KV tensors before/after quant/dequant in runtime (ephemeral flag --debug-kv-dumps).
- [ ] Run fp16 vs q8_0 diffs for the 5 diverging cases and save token-by-token scores. Put in results/jamie/diffcases/
- [ ] Try rotary_rescale=true and re-run single long sample.
- [ ] Schedule 2-hour slot with Maya to triage quant-induced drift (afternoon).

IDEAS / HYPOTHESES (brainstorm):
- Maybe the quant kernel uses per-tensor scale but we need per-head scale for some attention layers (try per-head quant in constrained layers).
- Could use a hybrid: keep first 4 transformer layers in fp16, quant rest; test unit economics vs quality.
- Use prefix caching aggressively for short-chat buckets, but disable for long sessions when q8_0 is active. Might buy latency without compounding drift.

METRICS TO CAPTURE (for today):
- CPU/GPU utilization trace (30s granularity).
- Token-level KL between fp16 and q8_0 for each sample.
- PPL proxy on holdout, hallucination rate, latency p50/p95/p99.

FOLLOWUPS / NOTES TO SELF: 
- If rotary_rescale fixes drift, file an infra issue to make it opt-in per-model.
- If drift persists, capture minimal repro and open a PR with failing unit test for quant kernel (helpful for upstream team).
- Keep the prompt tweaks minimal — prefer quant fixes over prompt surgery for now.

RANDOM TODO (small):
- [ ] Push results to Google Drive folder: shared_drives/engineering/applied-ml/quant-results/2026-03-13 (manual upload).
- [ ] Add a short note for the Console team: "q8_0: potential long-session drift" with initial numbers.

END OF DAY / QUICK RETROSPECT (placeholder):
- Fill this after triage meeting with Maya. Will note whether drift was config bug or numerical instability.

----
Scratchy bits, commands and partial outputs kept here so I can grep later. Not intended for sharing as-is.

journaled-by: Jamie Park (eng-applied-ml)
